transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (HavenAI CTO), Liam O'Connor (Infra Lead), Priya Singh (ML Eng)
Recording link: https://redwood.app/meetings/CRM-45872 (placeholder)
Shared artifacts: 1) Redwood Dedicated one-pager (link), 2) security pack (link), 3) benchmark spreadsheet (link)

Summary:
HavenAI is evaluating moving a multi-tenant customer-facing generation pipeline from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to either Redwood Hosted or Redwood Dedicated. Main drivers: predictable latency, cost control at scale, and data residency. They run a mixture of RAG + instruction-following generation, use vLLM in-house for some workloads, and rely heavily on a set of evals/QA prompts to validate output parity. They want to understand compatibility (TGI/vLLM vs Redwood runtime), quantization/throughput tradeoffs, and security/compliance (SSO, KMS, SOC2).

Topics covered: discovery of stack, traffic patterns, current costs, compatibility concerns (vLLM/TGI), eval parity, dedicated capacity sizing, security requirements, rollout plan.

Transcript:
00:00 Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm samira from redwood, we got diego from se here too. how's everyone?
00:03 Maya: hey thanks, yeah excited. quick apology, timezone juggling but good to be here.
00:06 Diego: hey all, will try to keep the technical bits concise then we can dig in.
00:10 Samira: cool, quick agenda — understand your current stack and goals, talk high-level about dedicated vs hosted, compatibility and security, then next steps. Maya, can you kick us off on what you're running today?
00:20 Maya: sure. so we run a customer-facing assistant product, about 2M monthly active users, peaks at 350 rps across many routes. currently all on OpenAI API (gpt-4o-ish) for generation and embeddings. we use a hybrid approach — embeddings cached in redis, and generation via OpenAI with local prefix caching. we're also experimenting with vLLM in our infra for lower-latency bursts. main pain points are cost predictability, some latency spikes during scaling, and data residency requests from EU customers.
00:45 Liam: and from infra side, we're trying to reduce egress and token costs; our monthly spend on OpenAI has grown 3x in 9 months. we want an option to reserve capacity and get consistent tail latency.
00:55 Samira: makes sense. when you say vLLM experiments, are you running your own model weights on-prem or in cloud?
01:00 Priya: primarily cloud GPUs, self-hosted vLLM with TGI layer for some custom models. for a few high-throughput routes we use a trimmed Llama variant, and we've seen good perf but engineering overhead is high. hope to reduce ops surface while keeping eval parity.
01:18 Diego: okay, good context. two quick clarifying Qs — what's your SLO for P95 latency and what volume do you expect to put on dedicated if we did that?
01:25 Maya: P95 target is ~250-300ms for the small chat flows, and up to 600ms for longchain generative tasks. Initially we want to move 30-40% of traffic to Dedicated as a canary — roughly 75 rps sustained with spikes to 200 rps. If it looks good, scale to 100% in 2-3 months.
01:45 Samira: great. low-level compatibility — you mentioned TGI/vLLM. Diego, do you want to walk through how Redwood handles model variants and whether we support the same APIs?
01:53 Diego: sure. at a high level, Redwood Dedicated runs an optimized serving runtime that supports standard model artifact formats. many teams using vLLM/TGI export models with HF transformer weights or GGML-style artifacts; we support those common formats and have a model-onboarding process. caveat: some custom TGI plugins or non-standard tokenizer configs need slight adjustments. our SE team can run the onboarding and a quick parity eval.
02:18 Priya: that is key — our eval suite has 1200 prompts, and slight tokenizer differences have changed outputs before. how do you guarantee parity?
02:27 Diego: parity guarantee is tough — we aim for functional parity. we run your eval set and surface delta metrics: token-level diffs, semantic similarity, and business-critical fail cases. if tokenizer mismatch shows up, we can align tokenizers or use the same HF tokenizer artifact. also quantization can change outputs; we recommend a staged approach — fp16 -> q4_0 -> q4_k_m, measure quality vs throughput.
02:50 Liam: what's the expected latency improvement vs our self-hosted vLLM? we saw 120ms median but higher p95 during GC and autoscale.
02:58 Diego: depends on model size and batching. our Dedicated pools use continuous batching and KV cache routing which typically improves GPU utilization and reduces cost per token; for small chat prompts we often match or beat self-hosted p95 because we control the runtime kernels and batching policies. for heavy long context tasks, throughput can be higher on dedicated pools but careful config needed to meet strict p95.
03:20 Maya: ok, security — we need SOC2, SSO (SAML ok), audit logs, KMS/HSM for encryption keys, and EU data residency. do you support a private control plane?
03:33 Samira: yes — Redwood Private is our VPC/on-prem option; Dedicated can be in a customer VPC with private networking. we have SOC2 Type II, ISO docs in the security pack Diego will share. we integrate with KMS providers and support customer-managed keys for private deployments.
03:50 Priya: and network egress — if we move from OpenAI to dedicated in the same cloud region can that reduce cross-region costs?
03:57 Diego: absolutely. colocating Dedicated instances in your EU region will reduce egress and residency concerns. we also support peering and private endpoints.
04:05 Samira: business question — what's your timeline and evaluation criteria?
04:07 Maya: timeline: PoC within 3 weeks, 2-week benchmark, then pilot for 30% of traffic in November. eval criteria: cost per 1k tokens (including infra and egress), p95 latency vs baseline, and output parity defined as <=3% business-critical regressions on our eval set.
04:25 Samira: that aligns with our standard migration path. we'll propose a Dedicated sizing for 75 rps sustained with burst capacity and an autoscale config. we'll also include pricing for a 6 or 12-month commit.
04:35 Priya: for the PoC, can we bring our model artifacts from vLLM/TGI and run them on your runtime? we want to test tokenizer and quantization differences.
04:42 Diego: yes — we typically ask customers to provide model weights and a small sample of prompts. we do onboarding to reproduce your inference pipeline flags. also, we'll run the eval suite and produce a delta report. expect to see slight variations with quantized configs; we'll provide recommendations and, if needed, custom kernel toggles.
04:59 Liam: curious about fallback and reliability — if Dedicated is full or degraded, can it route to Hosted or another region?
05:05 Samira: yes, smart routing is a core feature — can route by latency/capacity and fallback to hosted or another Dedicated cluster. we can also set canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies to avoid outages.
05:16 Maya: procurement — contract and compliance due diligence usually takes 3-4 weeks. pricing needs to be granular because our finance wants a clear unit economics model.
05:25 Samira: we'll include a cost modeling spreadsheet and examples of unit costs at different utilization levels. Diego will attach typical perf numbers for comparable model sizes.
05:33 Priya: small nit — do you support function/tool-calling or structured outputs at runtime? our product relies on a tool-calling pattern to external services.
05:40 Diego: yes, Redwood RPC supports streaming, function/tool calling, and structured JSON outputs. there are SDK helpers we can share.
05:47 Maya: one more — what's the ops handoff like, do you provide runbooks and on-call support for Dedicated?
05:52 Samira: Dedicated includes a managed ops SLA, incident runbooks, and optional 24/7 support add-on. we also provide tracing hooks and cost/latency dashboards via Redwood Console.
06:02 (brief cross talk)
06:10 Samira: okay i want to recap and capture next steps — Diego will share the security pack and onboarding checklist, i'll send pricing and committed capacity options, and we should schedule the benchmark run with Priya next week. does that sound right?
06:21 Maya: yes. can you also share an example E2E benchmark report?
06:24 Diego: will do, sending an anonymized benchmark report from a similar customer.
06:28 Priya: i'll assemble the 1200-prompt eval subset and send sample model artifacts (tokenizer + model weights) to the onboarding bucket.
06:35 Samira: great — tentative follow-up week of 2026-10-29, i'll propose times. thanks everyone.
06:40 Maya: thanks all.
